name: Indian Diabetic Retinopathy Image Dataset (IDRiD)
description: IDRiD is the first publicly-released DR dataset with both pixel-level annotation of typical DR lesions (microaneurysms, hemorrhages, hard exudates, soft exudates) and image-level disease severity grading (5 DR grades + 3 DME risk grades). 516 fundus colour photographs of Indian patients acquired at the Eye Clinic of Sushrushti Hospital, Aurangabad, India. First fixture in the OCI Platform catalogue — references the upstream Grand Challenge distribution; PR C will mirror the bytes into the platform's RESTRICTED storage tier with pre-signed URLs.

rai:dataCollection: Acquired at a single eye clinic in Aurangabad (Maharashtra, India) over 2009-2017. All studies are colour fundus photographs of patients undergoing routine DR screening; no incentive given to participants. Macula-centred field of view, captured at 4288x2848 px on a Kowa VX-10α retinal camera.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two ophthalmologists with >25 years of clinical experience independently labelled each image. Disagreements were adjudicated by a third senior ophthalmologist. For sub-task A (lesion segmentation), pixel-level masks were drawn per lesion class using ITK-SNAP. For sub-task B, image-level grades were assigned per the International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy and Diabetic Macular Edema Disease Severity Scales.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: ITK-SNAP for segmentation; custom CSV for grading.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three ophthalmologists with >25 years of clinical experience each.
rai:dataBiases: Single-site cohort skews toward an Indian patient population recruited at a tertiary eye clinic. Generalisation to other ethnicities, primary-care settings, or different camera hardware is untested. Class imbalance favours mild-to-moderate DR over severe and proliferative grades.
rai:dataLimitations: Macula-centred only; no peripheral fundus, no ultra-wide-field imaging, no OCT or OCT-A. Not suitable for paediatric retina, retinopathy of prematurity, or non-DR pathologies. The 516-image scale is too small for training large models from scratch.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No direct identifiers. Patient age and sex were not retained alongside the images.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of: DR severity grading classifiers, DME risk classifiers, lesion segmentation models (microaneurysms, hemorrhages, hard/soft exudates, optic disc).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Hosted by Grand Challenge platform since 2018. No content updates expected. Original IEEE Standards Association DSC2018 archive available for long-term preservation.
bio:dataAcquisitionProtocol: Macula-centred 50° field of view, captured on a Kowa VX-10α non-mydriatic retinal camera. All images saved as JPEG at native sensor resolution 4288x2848.
bio:consentNotes: Routine clinical screening; informed consent for research use captured at acquisition per Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) guidelines.
